verbalization: Dalotuzumab is implicated in targeting multiple pathways that ultimately converge on Serine/threonine-protein kinase ATR. The evidence suggests that Dalotuzumab may act through distinct molecular mechanisms, yet all pathways lead to the same target, ATR. The first path links Dalotuzumab to Liver X receptor (LXR), which is targeted by Cornusalterin E, and this chain culminates in ATR. The second and third paths connect Dalotuzumab to Voltage-dependent L-type calcium channel subunit beta-3, which is targeted by methyl (Z)-7-hexadecenoate and gamma-aminobutyric acid, both of which also target ATR. These diverse targets suggest that Dalotuzumab may exert its effects through multiple routes, but all ultimately engage ATR. The integration of these pathways highlights a potential mechanism where Dalotuzumab influences cellular processes by modulating signaling pathways that converge on ATR, possibly through the regulation of gene expression or downstream signaling cascades. The shared involvement of ATR across these pathways underscores the importance of this kinase in the biological response to Dalotuzumab, though the exact mechanism of ATR activation remains to be fully elucidated.
